summary: Gustav Haloun was a sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Vienna, Leipzig under August Conrady, and Prague. He held positions at Prague, Bonn, Halle, Berlin, and Göttingen, before serving as Cambridge's Chair of Chinese Language and History (1938–1951).

Gustav Mensching was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Marburg under Rudolf Otto. He taught Hans-Joachim Klimkeit and Demosthenes Savramis, and held academic posts at the University of Latvia (1927–1936) and the University of Bonn (1936).

Gustav Roth was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Breslau, Leipzig, Halle-Wittenberg, Munich, and Patna, working under Paul Thieme and Gaurinath Sastri, among others. He was an Akademischer Oberrat at Göttingen (1965–1981) and Director at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).

Gustav Salomon Oppert was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the universities of Bonn, Leipzig, and Halle-Wittenberg, as well as the Berlin University of the Arts, where he later held an academic post from circa 1895 to 1908.

Gustave Lanson studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Faculty of Arts of Paris. He taught at Lycée Charlemagne, Collège Louis-le-Grand, the University of Paris and its Faculty of Arts (~1900–1927), and Columbia University (~1911–1912).
Gustavo Benavides is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He held an academic post at Villanova University, attested in 1995 and 2004.
Guus Kroonen is a linguist who earned his doctorate under Alexander Lubotsky. He held academic posts at the University of Copenhagen around 2013 and at Leiden University in 2016.

Guy G. Stroumsa studied at Paris, Hebrew University of Jerusalem, EPHE, and Harvard, learning under Emmanuel Levinas. A religious studies scholar, he taught at Hebrew University (1978–2009) and was Professor of the Study of the Abrahamic Religions at Oxford (2009–2013).

Guy Newland is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, studied under teachers including Donald S. Lopez, Jr., and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Central Michigan University (attested 1996–2010).
Gyal Rong Tendzin Drakpa was a scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Patrul Rinpoche.

Gyatsho Tshering, a Tibetology scholar educated at the University of Calcutta, was a founder of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, serving as its Acting Director in 1972 and as Director from 1974 to 1998.

Gyoei Fukuda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tendai Daigakurin. He served as president of Taisho University (~1926–1944) and held posts at the University of Tokyo (1928) and Toyo University.
Gyoko Iotani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1968–1978). He spent his career at Rissho University as an assistant professor (~1984–1991) and professor (~1991).
Gyomay Kubose was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Otani University under Haya Akegarasu from circa 1936 to 1941, and later taught Brad Warner.
Gyosho Takahashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1992) and Minobusan University (attested 1996).
Gyoshu Chojo is a Buddhist studies scholar who held professorships at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1996) and on the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Minobusan University (attested 2001).
Gyula Ortutay studied at the University of Szeged (1928–1934). He taught András Róna-Tas and held a post at Nyugat.

Gyurme Dorje studied Tibetology and Buddhist studies at Edinburgh and SOAS, completing a PhD under Philip Denwood and training with Dudjom Rinpoche and others. He held fellowships at SOAS and UCL (1991–1996) and worked as a translator for Tsadra Foundation (2007–2020).
Gyurme Pema Tekchok studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

György Hazai was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University from 1949 to 1954 and worked at the Institut für Orientforschung between roughly 1963 and 1983.
